title: Python: the attribute-write rule (DEC-303 (a25)): a write that shadows an attribute target must not resolve to the def
description: Filed record-only under opum-doc's ruling ODOC-640 (opum-ai/opum-doc#2065) from the hold list carried in GCLI-86 and GCLI-132. Rule, DEC-303 (a25) (2026-11-25, opum-ai/opum-doc#1966, ODOC-640; full text in the GCLI-86 'HANDOFF 9 ADDENDUM' note), by (a22) item 2: an attribute write is a binding of that attribute. A write that shadows the target (self.m = f; self.m(); k.m = f; k.m(); self.__class__ = Other; the in-module monkeypatches mod.f = g, Cls.meth = g) must not resolve to the def: calls through self, cls or Cls to that attribute become unresolved, counted as multiply bound, subclasses inherit the treatment. Precision work: fixtures red before and green after, mutants observed red, and the five-pin delta. Any in-repo edge created or removed comes to opum-doc before the clear. Not started; the brief comes from the leader. Order per (a28): this task, then NB-b, then step 5.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Read the (a25) rule text in the GCLI-86 note and DEC-303 (a25) before building; do not widen it

One refused fixture per shape (self.m, cls.m, Cls.m anywhere in the module, mod.f in the defining module and in an importer, self.__class__, x.m on an R4 or E1 local), each with its positive twin, each measured against dev by running both
Mutants observed red; the five-pin delta with every created or removed in-repo edge reported to opum-doc before the clear

plan: 1. Fixtures first in test/python-hops.test.ts (describe GCLI-140): one refused fixture per (a25) shape — self.m, cls.m, Cls.m, mod.f in the importer and in the defining module, self.__class__, type(self), x.m on a 6d/R4 local, setattr literal — each with a positive twin; run on dev to record red-before.
2. Walker: record raw attribute writes (assignment, augmented, for, with-as, comprehension targets; setattr with a literal name) as (base callee descriptor, attr, scope, site).

3. Resolver: classify each write at first call resolution into class attr writes (receiver param, class name), module attr writes (import-bound module path), or local name attr writes (binding scope); gate setattr on the unshadowed builtin.

4. Guards: methodLookup refuses a non-super lookup whose MRO carries the attr write; localClassOfReceiver refuses on a __class__ write; knownClassOf/localConstructedClass refuse a written local attribute; resolveModuleAttribute/resolveModuleChain refuse a written module attribute.

5. Prove: fixtures green on head, red on dev; a mutant per guard observed red; differential over constructed sources varying binder and read positions with a positive control; five-pin cmp; report created/removed in-repo edges to the leader before the PR.
implementationNotes: BUILT on dev 57ba445 (branch not yet pushed; five-pin delta reported to the leader before the PR, per the brief). Files: src/python/calls.ts (walker records attribute writes; Resolver classifies them and refuses), test/python-hops.test.ts (describe GCLI-140, 15 fixtures). Walker: assignment/augmented/for/with-as/comprehension attribute targets and setattr(obj, "m", v) with a literal name are recorded as (base descriptor, attr, scope, site); a shadowed setattr is not the builtin. Resolver: a write to a method receiver lands on the enclosing class, a class name (module-level or local) on that class, an import-bound module name on that module file, anything else on the binding local; guards in methodLookup (non-super, MRO-wide), localClassOfReceiver (__class__), resolveAttributeCall's known-class path and localConstructedClass (x.m), resolveModuleAttribute, moduleBindingGate and resolveModuleChain (mod.f). RED-BEFORE, measured by running both heads: every refused fixture gives dev inRepo 1 with the wrong edge (self.m, cls.m, Cls.m direct/instance/class-body, mod.f in the importer/defining/star/reexport/submodule shapes, self.__class__ and type(self), x.m single-binding and R4, setattr local and self) and head receiver 1 or nameNotBound 1 with no edge; every positive twin, the non-literal setattr, the shadowed setattr and the different-attribute cases resolve identically on both. MUTANTS (11, one at a time, each restored): class-guard 6 red; local-6d 2; local-r4 1; class-write 1; module-gate 1 (re-export); module-chain 1 (submodule); setattr-record 1; setattr-shadowed 1; receiver-classify 4; classSymbol-classify 3; module-attr-top GREEN (a guard kept for the recursive hop path in resolveModuleAttribute; the chain check and the gate check already refuse every input the corpus reaches, so it is named untested rather than claimed proved). DIFFERENTIAL: 31-case dev-vs-head probe over the new shapes (binder positions: same method, another method, a base class, module level, a class body, a function; read positions: same method, another method, a subclass, a constructed call, an alias) with twins as positive controls: all twins identical on both heads, all write cases refused only on head. The archived 1394-source corpus is IDENTICAL dev vs head (it carries no attribute-write shapes). FIVE PINS (flask 49943b5a, httpx 7cff5f79, jinja 5ef70112, rich 3a109ccd, tqdm 9cf5a12b): 0 in-repo edges created, 0 removed; httpx and jinja byte-identical; flask external 1221->1219 and receiver 1489->1491; rich external 2514->2512 and receiver 1407->1409; tqdm external 1167->1163 and receiver 854->858; 95 receiver sites change reason instance-attribute -> needs-inference (same bin, no edge). Reason for the refusals is needs-inference; module attribut writes land in nameNotBound, the existing bucket for an unresolved module attribute. Full suite 1260 pass, typecheck clean, lint one pre-existing warning, format:check clean.
